newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares drop in bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares drop in bearish sentiment.

text.p: Jordanian shares maintained a downward trend on Sunday on profit-taking and disappointing half-year results, despite some local portfolio buying of blue-chip drug firms, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.34 percent to 164.01 points in turnover worth 601,646 dinars ($848,583).

Brokers said the bourse eased despite some orders for leading drug firms which performed well during the first half of 1997. They attributed the downward pressure to profit-taking in some shares that had recently risen and disappointing half-year results for many companies.
But two blue-chip drug firms, Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturing and Dar al-Dawa, saw mostly locally inspired trade, underpinned by favourable half-year results.
The two shares rose 0.04 dinars to 4.14 dinars and 5.44 dinars respectively.
Jordan Cement Factory, a focus of foreign fund interest over the last few months, shed 0.03 dinars to 3.97 dinars in low volume worth only 69,225 dinars.
Overall 13 shares rose and 22 fell. A further 14 traded but closed unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, fell 0.10 percent to 80.51 points, 3.46 percent down since the start of the year.
